transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Ethan Park (Redwood AE), Nina Gomez (Redwood SE), Rahul Mehta (CTO, SolaceAI), Claire Zhou (ML Eng), Tomas Ortega (Infra)

Auto-summary (may be rough): SolaceAI currently on OpenAI + some self-hosted vLLM for bursty on-prem needs. Evaluating Redwood Dedicated or Private for predictable latency and cost, plus KMS/VPC controls. They want eval parity and to understand migration effort and compatibility with TGI/vLLM stacks.

[00:00:00] Ethan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Ethan from Redwood, AE on the account, with Nina who is our SE. How's everyone doing?
[00:00:10] Rahul: Good, thanks. Quick intros, I'm Rahul, CTO. Claire is our ML lead and Tomas is infra. We're short on time so want to get to specifics — latency, cost, security.
[00:00:25] Nina: Great, we'll aim to cover migration surface, compatibility with vLLM/TGI, and what Dedicated/Private look like for you.
[00:00:38] Claire: To start, we're running most traffic through OpenAI right now. We also have some internal models served via vLLM on k8s for really low-latency endpoints. Main driver is cost predictability and keeping P95 latency under 200ms for the assistant flow.
[00:00:55] Tomas: Also need to hit data residency and KMS — certain prompts touch PHI-ish data, so encryption and audit logs are musts.
[00:01:05] Ethan: Understood. High level: Redwood Dedicated gives you reserved capacity with predictable throughput, and Private gives you VPC/on-prem control with customer-managed keys. Both have RBAC, audit logs, and KMS integrations.
[00:01:22] Rahul: Can you run through the migration path from OpenAI? We're worried about eval parity — same responses and hallucination profiles.
[00:01:34] Nina: Totally. Two parts: model compatibility and prompt/eval parity. For model compatibility, we support the common model families we'd mapped in our catalog — and we can run identical checkpoints or close variants. For Parity we run your eval set through Redwood and compare metrics (accuracy, helpfulness, toxic flags) and statistically test drift.
[00:01:55] Claire: How about customers who are using TGI or vLLM? We want to reuse some of our infra and inference pipelines.
[00:02:05] Nina: We see that a lot. Redwood can accept the same tokenization and model artifacts in many cases. There are sometimes runtime differences — vLLM uses different KV cache patterns, and TGI might have slightly different sampling defaults. We surface those in the benchmark and give recommendations — e.g., quantization profiles, kernel selection.
[00:02:28] Rahul: Any caveats with function calling or streaming? Our assistant uses streaming heavily.
[00:02:33] Nina: Streaming is first-class in Redwood. Function/tool calling semantics are supported; we also allow structured output enforcement. Minor SDK differences but we provide compatibility layers and quickstart snippets.
[00:02:45] Tomas: Performance wise, with Dedicated, what kind of p95 and throughput can we expect compared to OpenAI? Numbers please.
[00:02:53] Ethan: Ballpark — depends on model and quantization. For a 7B optimized on GPU with our kernels and batching you often see p95 in the 80–150ms range for short prompts. We can do a benchmark using your prompt set to get apples-to-apples vs your current OpenAI calls.
[00:03:10] Claire: Do you support mixed precision / INT8 quantization? We've been testing that on vLLM.
[00:03:16] Nina: Yes — quantization profiles are configurable. We recommend a few presets depending on accuracy tolerance; Redwood Optimize will suggest which quant profiles to try based on your evals.
[00:03:26] Rahul: About fallback: if Dedicated capacity is full, what's the behavior?
[00:03:30] Ethan: You can configure smart routing: fallback to a higher-latency hosted tier or alternative model variants. We also do canary rollouts and A/B tests for new versions.
[00:03:40] Tomas: On security, SOC2 is needed for procurement. Does Redwood have SOC2 + ISO?
[00:03:45] Ethan: Yes, SOC2 Type II and ISO 27001 are available — we'll share the package. For KMS integration, we support customer-managed keys with HSM integrations on Private.
[00:03:58] Claire: How intrusive is Private? We have some air-gapped needs for certain customers.
[00:04:03] Nina: Private can be VPC-hosted or on-prem. On-prem is more involved — it's packaged but requires our ops + your infra team. We usually scope a POC for 4–8 weeks for that.
[00:04:14] Rahul: Could you walk us through what the PoC/benchmark would look like?
[00:04:18] Nina: Sure: step one, collect your eval prompt set and traffic profile. Step two, run a parity benchmark — same prompts against your OpenAI baseline and Redwood Dedicated instance. We'll measure latency (p50/p95), token cost estimates, and quality metrics. Step three, iterate on quantization and batching settings. Step four, pilot on a subset of traffic and verify monitoring/alerts.
[00:04:40] Claire: About comparability with vLLM — we run a lot of our staging on vLLM with custom KV cache patterns; will Redwood preserve same caching behavior?
[00:04:49] Nina: We have a KV cache implementation but the semantics can vary. We'll capture your expected warmup patterns and ensure the cache warming + continuous batching roughly match your latency SLOs. In practice we instrument differences and sometimes tweak batch windows.
[00:05:05] Rahul: Pricing — do you have per-token and also reserved capacity commits?
[00:05:10] Ethan: Hosted is usage-based; Dedicated is reserved capacity with monthly/annual commitments and typically better unit economics. We'll send a sizing sheet so you can see cost per token under your load.
[00:05:20] Tomas: Any lock-in risk? If we want to revert to OpenAI or other hosted, how easy is that?
[00:05:26] Nina: We support model variants and fallbacks; our API is designed to be similar to what you're used to. We also provide export instructions for prompts and eval results. But obviously switching has operational work — the PoC is a good way to validate rollback paths.
[00:05:40] Claire: For function calling, do we need to rewrite call signatures?
[00:05:44] Nina: Usually minor changes in SDKs only. We'll provide adapter snippets.
[00:05:50] Rahul: Any customers who've migrated from OpenAI and kept parity?
[00:05:54] Ethan: Yes, a few. We ran a parity bench for one fintech where outputs matched within confidence intervals after tuning quantization and sampling. We'll share anonymized case notes.
[00:06:07] Rahul: What's the typical timeline from pilot to dedicated prod?
[00:06:11] Ethan: If a pilot shows parity and infra is ready, 6–12 weeks is common for Dedicated; on-prem Private can be longer depending on approvals.
[00:06:20] Tomas: Network egress and VPC peering — we need to know data paths for compliance.
[00:06:24] Nina: For Private, all traffic stays inside your VPC; for Dedicated we support VPC endpoints and private networking. We'll provide architecture diagrams.
[00:06:34] Claire: One technical question — you mentioned kernel selection. How much of that is automatic vs manual tuning?
[00:06:39] Nina: Mostly automatic. The runtime profiles workload and picks optimized kernels. For edge cases we can manual-tune on the Dedicated pool.
[00:06:47] Rahul: Regarding eval parity, what metrics should we collect? We track exact-match, BLEU-ish metrics for code, hallucination rate, and a subjective helpfulness score.
[00:06:58] Nina: Perfect. We'll ask for your allowed metrics and set up a quickscript to run them. We'll compare distributions and run statistical tests.
[00:07:08] Rahul: Any differences with Anthropic models? We've evaluated Claude for a vertical.
[00:07:13] Ethan: Model behavior varies but the process is the same — benchmark side-by-side. We can map model equivalents in our catalog where available.
[00:07:21] Claire: For our vLLM workloads, we sometimes use custom compilation flags. Will Redwood take those into account?
[00:07:27] Nina: We'll ask for your runtime flags; in Dedicated we can tune the runtime. If needed, we can approximate with similar kernel parameters.
[00:07:36] Tomas: SLA questions: what uptime do you promise and how do you calculate p95 latency across multi-tenant Dedicated?
[00:07:42] Ethan: SLA numbers are in the Dedicated contract. We measure latency at the route level and give per-route dashboards. We'll include sample SLO definitions in the docs.
[00:07:54] Rahul: Who will be our primary SE contact?
[00:07:57] Ethan: Nina will lead the technical side.
[00:08:00] Claire: Quick triage: what are the blockers for us? For procurement: SOC2 + architecture; for ML: eval parity; for infra: network + KMS.
[00:08:10] Ethan: Sounds right — we'll prioritize sending SOC2 and architecture diagram, and Nina will own the parity benchmark plan.
[00:08:18] Rahul: Can you put an example benchmark template in the docs so procurement can see it?
[00:08:22] Ethan: Yep. We'll attach a template and the pricing/sizing sheet.
[00:08:28] (small cross-talk)
[00:08:35] Claire: A few practicals — can snapshots of logs be exported for legal audits?
[00:08:40] Nina: Yes, audit logs can be exported; for Private you have direct access. For Dedicated we stream logs to your S3/equivalent via a connector.
[00:08:50] Rahul: Any gotchas with rate limits when doing canaries?
[00:08:54] Ethan: You can define routes with throttles and special routing policies. We'll help set those up.
[00:09:02] Tomas: I'm curious about cost modeling — what inputs do you need?
[00:09:07] Nina: Prompt sizes, token counts, QPS, concurrency, model family, and target latency determine batch sizing and cost; send us sample traces.
[00:09:18] Rahul: Ok, let's talk about next steps.
[00:09:21] Ethan: Proposed actions: Ethan send SOC2 + security pack + Dedicated sizing. Nina propose benchmark plan and list of test prompts. Rahul share prompt set and traffic profile. Then SE-run parity benchmark and report.
[00:09:35] Claire: Timeline — can we get the docs and plan by end of next week?
[00:09:38] Ethan: Yes, we'll aim for that.
[00:09:41] Rahul: One more — we use a lot of streaming, so can we do a micro-benchmark first for streaming 1000 requests?
[00:09:49] Nina: Yes, include that in the benchmark.
[00:09:52] Ethan: Anything else?
[00:09:55] (silence)
[00:10:00] Ethan: Alright, recap: We'll send security docs and pricing, propose benchmark, customer shares prompts and traffic profile, schedule SE deep dive.
[00:10:10] Rahul: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.

[00:10:20] End meeting notes:
- Agreed deliverables and owners as in action items.
- Redwood to run parity benchmark comparing OpenAI baseline and Dedicated instance; focus on latency (p50/p95), cost estimates, and output parity metrics.
- Customer provided constraints: p95 < 200ms target for assistant, SOC2/KMS for PHI-ish data, VPC/private networking for certain flows.

Notes on transcript quality: auto-generated, medium quality; some proper nouns may be mis-transcribed (e.g., k-v cache spelled "k-v cash").

Links mentioned: Redwood Dedicated sizing sheet (link to be sent), SOC2 pack (link to be sent), benchmark template (to be attached).

- Ethan: Send pricing + Dedicated sizing + SOC2 pack by 2026-03-06.
- Nina: Draft benchmark plan and test prompts, propose dates for the run by 2026-03-05.
- Rahul/Claire: Share sample prompt set, recent traces, and success criteria by 2026-03-05.
